title_en: Arrangement of the Supreme People's Court on Mutual Entrustment of Service of Judicial Documents and Taking of Evidence in Civil and Commercial Cases Between the Courts of the Mainland and the Macao Special Administrative Region

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Arrangement shall apply to the mutual entrustment of service of judicial documents and the taking of evidence between the People's Courts of the Mainland and the courts of the Macao Special Administrative Region in civil and commercial cases (including labor dispute cases on the Mainland and civil labor cases in the Macao Special Administrative Region).

Article 2 The mutual entrustment between the two sides for the service of judicial documents and the taking of evidence shall be conducted through the Higher People's Courts and the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region. The Supreme People's Court and the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region may directly entrust each other with the service of judicial documents and the taking of evidence.
After consultation with the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region, the Supreme People's Court may authorize certain Intermediate People's Courts and Primary People's Courts to mutually entrust the service of judicial documents and the taking of evidence with the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 3 The mutual entrustment between the two sides for the service of judicial documents and the taking of evidence shall be transmitted electronically through the judicial assistance network platform between the Mainland and Macao; where electronic transmission through the judicial assistance network platform is not possible, postal service shall be used.
Judicial documents, evidentiary materials and other documents transmitted electronically through the judicial assistance network platform shall be ensured to be complete, authentic and unalterable.
Judicial documents, evidentiary materials and other documents transmitted electronically through the judicial assistance network platform shall have the same legal effect as the originals.

Article 4 Upon receipt of a letter of entrustment from the court of the other party, each Higher People's Court and the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall immediately transmit the letter of entrustment and the attached judicial documents and related documents to the court that is competent to accomplish the entrusted matter according to the laws of its jurisdiction.
Where the entrusted court finds that the entrusted matter has problems such as incomplete materials or insufficient information that affect its completion of the entrusted matter, it shall promptly notify the entrusting court to supplement the materials or provide an explanation.
Where an authorized Intermediate People's Court or Primary People's Court, upon receipt of a letter of entrustment from the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region, considers that the matter is not within its jurisdiction, it shall report to the Higher People's Court for handling.
Article 5 A letter of entrustment shall be submitted in Chinese. Where the attached judicial documents and other related documents are not in Chinese, a Chinese translation shall be provided.

Article 6 The entrusting court shall make the entrustment request within a reasonable period so as to ensure that the entrusted court, after receiving the letter of entrustment, timely completes the entrusted matter.
The entrusted court shall give priority to handling the entrusted matter. The time limit for completing the entrusted matter shall not exceed two months from the date of receipt of the letter of entrustment for the service of documents, and shall not exceed three months from the date of receipt of the letter of entrustment for the taking of evidence.

Article 7 The entrusted court shall execute the entrusted matter in accordance with the laws of its jurisdiction. Where the entrusting court requests that the entrusted matter be executed in a special manner, the entrusted court may execute it in the special manner if it considers that the special manner does not contravene the laws of its jurisdiction.

Article 8 The entrusting court shall not be obliged to pay the fees and taxes incurred by the entrusted court in serving judicial documents and taking evidence. However, in accordance with the laws of its jurisdiction, the entrusted court shall have the right, when taking evidence, to require the entrusting court to advance the fees of expert evaluators, witnesses and interpreters, as well as the expenses incurred from the special manner of service of judicial documents and taking of evidence requested by the entrusting court in the letter of entrustment.

Article 9 The entrusted court shall not, on the grounds that it has exclusive jurisdiction over the civil or commercial case being heard by the entrusting court under the laws of its jurisdiction, or that it does not recognize the right to bring an action with respect to the requested matter, refuse to execute the entrusted matter.
Where the entrusted court, when executing the entrusted matter, finds that the matter is not within the functions and powers of the courts, or the Mainland People's Court considers that executing the entrusted matter on the Mainland would violate its fundamental legal principles or social public interest, or the court of the Macao Special Administrative Region considers that executing the entrusted matter in the Macao Special Administrative Region would violate its fundamental legal principles or public order, it may refuse to execute the matter, but shall promptly explain in writing to the entrusting court the reasons for the refusal.
II. Service of Judicial Documents

Article 10 Where the entrusting court requests the service of judicial documents, it shall issue a letter of entrustment affixed with its seal or signed by a judge, and shall state in the letter of entrustment the name of the entrusting organ, the name or designation and detailed address of the person on whom service is to be made, and the nature of the case. Where the entrusting court requests service in a special manner or has matters requiring special attention, it shall indicate such matters in the letter of entrustment.

Article 11 Where the entrustment is made by postal service, the letter of entrustment and the attached judicial documents and other related documents shall be made in duplicate; where there are two or more persons on whom service is to be made, a duplicate set shall be provided for each person.

Article 12 After the service of judicial documents has been completed, the People's Court on the Mainland shall issue a proof of service, and the court of the Macao Special Administrative Region shall issue a certificate of service. The proof of service and the certificate of service issued shall state the method, place and date of service and the identity of the recipient of the judicial documents, and shall be affixed with the seal of the court.
Where the entrusted court cannot accomplish service, it shall note on the proof of service or the certificate of service the reasons preventing service, the grounds for refusal and the date, and shall promptly reply in writing to the entrusting court.

Article 13 Regardless of whether the date of appearance or the time limit specified in the judicial documents of the entrusting court has already passed, the entrusted court shall still effect service.
Article 14 The entrusted court shall not bear legal liability for the content and consequences of the judicial documents and attached related documents entrusted for service by the entrusting court.

Article 15 For the purposes of this Arrangement, judicial documents on the Mainland include: copies of statements of prosecution, copies of statements of appeal, copies of statements of counterclaim, copies of statements of defense, powers of attorney, summonses, judgments, mediation documents, rulings, payment orders, decisions, notices, certificates, proofs of service, and other judicial documents and attached related documents; and in the Macao Special Administrative Region, include: copies of statements of prosecution, copies of statements of defense, copies of statements of counterclaim, copies of statements of appeal, statements, defense statements, declarations of opposition, rebuttals, applications, withdrawal petitions, admissions, settlement documents, property inventories, property division lists, settlement proposals, creditor agreements, summonses, notices, judge's instructions, writs, court permits, judgments, collegiate court judgments, certificates of service, and other judicial documents and attached related documents.
III. Taking of Evidence
Article 16 Evidence requested by the entrusting court to be taken may only be evidence used in connection with the litigation.

Article 18 The scope of taking evidence on behalf of the entrusting court includes: questioning parties, witnesses and expert evaluators on behalf of the entrusting court, conducting expert evaluation and judicial inspection on behalf of the entrusting court, and taking other evidence related to the litigation.

Article 19 Where the entrusting court makes a request, the entrusted court shall notify the entrusting court of the time and place of taking evidence so that the parties concerned and their litigation agents may be present.

Article 20 When executing an entrusted matter of taking evidence, the entrusted court may, upon the request of the entrusting court, allow judicial personnel of the entrusting court to be present. Where necessary, with the permission of the entrusted party, judicial personnel of the entrusting court may ask questions of witnesses, expert evaluators and other persons.

Article 21 After the entrusted court completes the entrusted matter of taking evidence, it shall give a written explanation to the entrusting court.
Where the entrusted court fails to complete the matter of taking evidence in whole or in part as requested by the entrusting court, it shall give a written explanation to the entrusting court of the reasons preventing the taking of evidence; if the entrustment was made by postal service, it shall promptly return the letter of entrustment and the attached documents.
Where a party or witness, in accordance with the laws of the entrusted party, refuses to testify or declines to provide testimony, the entrusted court shall notify the entrusting court in writing; if the entrustment was made by postal service, it shall promptly return the letter of entrustment and the attached documents.

Article 22 The entrusted court may, upon the request of the entrusting court and with the consent of the witnesses and expert evaluators, assist in arranging for witnesses and expert evaluators within its jurisdiction to appear in court in the other party's jurisdiction to testify.
During the period when witnesses and expert evaluators stay within the territory of the entrusting party, they shall not be criminally prosecuted or placed in custody on account of acts committed before their departure from the territory of the entrusted party or of judgments rendered against them within the territory of the entrusting party, shall not be deprived of property or have their identity documents withheld for the purpose of performing a penalty or other punishment, and shall not be subject to any restriction on their personal freedom in any manner.
Where witnesses and expert evaluators, after completing the required litigation acts and being free to leave the territory of the entrusting party, remain within the territory of the entrusting party for more than seven days, or leave the territory of the entrusting party and then return on their own accord, the immunity provided in the preceding paragraph shall terminate.
The expenses and compensation arising from witnesses and expert evaluators appearing in court before the entrusting court shall be advanced by the entrusting court.
For the purposes of this Article, persons appearing in court to testify also include parties in the Macao Special Administrative Region.

Article 23 The entrusted court may, upon the request of the entrusting court and with the consent of the witnesses and expert evaluators, assist in arranging for witnesses and expert evaluators within its jurisdiction to testify through video and audio.

Article 24 When the entrusted court takes evidence, the agents of the parties, witnesses, expert evaluators and other persons under investigation may be present.
IV. Supplementary Provisions
Article 25 The entrusted court may, upon the request of the entrusting court, inquire into and provide the relevant laws of its jurisdiction on behalf of the entrusting court.

Article 26 Where problems arise in the course of implementation of this Arrangement, they shall be resolved through consultation between the Supreme People's Court and the Court of Final Appeal of the Macao Special Administrative Region.
Where this Arrangement needs to be modified, the matter shall be resolved through consultation between the Supreme People's Court and the Macao Special Administrative Region.
Article 27 This Arrangement shall take effect as of September 15, 2001. The amended version of this Arrangement shall take effect as of March 1, 2020.
